sourcedFrom: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: A straight-blowback 5.7 x 28 mm carbine that feeds from a magazine lying along the top and ejects out of the bottom. It comes apart into five groups without tools, but only with the hammer cocked: once the cocking handle has been worked for the strip, the trigger is not touched. The moving parts get a few drops of lubricant. The hammer group and the magazine get none. Deep Clean adds the magazine, which FN lets you open if it is not the 10-round one.

steps.title: Read the marking on the barrel support
steps.action: Look at the rear left side of the barrel support. It should read PS90 cal 5.7x28. If it reads anything else, or your carbine does not look like the one FN draws, stop and get the book for the one you have. Move all ammunition away from the bench and put eye protection on.
steps.prose: FN's book describes the standard PS90 with the upper rail. If yours is another variant, or wears its own sight, FN put separate instructions in the shipping box, and those come first wherever they differ.
steps.quote: If your FN HERSTAL carbine has an inscription other than “PS90 cal 5.7x28” on the rear left side of the barrel support or if the external appearance of the carbine does not correspond to the illustrations of this manual, you must contact a FN Recommended Service Center / your departmental armorer or write us immediately to obtain the free owner’s manual that has been written specifically for your carbine.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — Caution block, p.2; Variants, p.14; §1, p.9

steps.title: Muzzle safe, selector to S
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep your fingers away from the trigger. Set the fire selector at S.
steps.prose: At S the trigger cannot be operated. It is still a mechanical device, and FN tells you never to rely on it completely, so S is where the clearing starts and not where it ends.
steps.quote: Set the fire selector at the position ‘S’ (safe).
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §4.5 Unloading the carbine, p.22; §1, p.6
steps.warn: Always assume that your carbine can be fired at any time, even with all safety mechanisms engaged.

steps.title: Magazine off the top
steps.action: Pull the magazine catch rearward to release the magazine, then lift the magazine away. Put it down away from the carbine.
steps.prose: The magazine comes off before the cocking handle moves. Left on, the next stroke of the handle feeds a round. Do not judge by the clear magazine body: FN says the last two cartridges, and the one in the chamber, cannot be seen while it is on the carbine.
steps.quote: Pull the magazine catch rearward in order to release the magazine and then remove the magazine.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §4.5 Unloading the carbine, p.23; §1, p.7
steps.warn: The magazine must therefore always be removed and the chamber cleared in order to ensure that the carbine is empty !

steps.title: Cocking handle, at least three full strokes
steps.action: Pull the cocking handle all the way back and release it, so that any cartridge in the chamber is extracted and thrown out. Do that at least three times.
steps.prose: Cases leave through the bottom of the frame, so leave room under the carbine and watch for one dropping out. Short strokes are the mistake: it has to go completely rearward each time.
steps.quote: Pull the cocking handle completely rearward and then release it in order to extract and eject the remaining cartridge from the chamber.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §4.5 Unloading the carbine, p.23

steps.title: Hold it back and look into the chamber
steps.action: Pull the cocking handle completely rearward and hold it there. Look down through the magazine opening into the chamber and see that there is no cartridge in it. If there is one, release the handle and pull it back again to eject it. When the chamber is empty, release the handle. Make sure the magazine is empty too.
steps.prose: Your hand is all that is holding it back, so keep the other hand out of the opening. The hammer is cocked after this. FN's own check goes on to put the selector at 1, pull the trigger in a safe direction to decock, and put the selector back at S. The strip cocks the hammer again, so leave the selector at S from here.
steps.quote: Through the magazine opening, look into the chamber of the carbine in order to ensure that there is no cartridge in the chamber.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §4.5 Unloading the carbine, p.23; §4.1 Safety checks, p.19

steps.title: Cock it, then leave the trigger alone
steps.action: With the magazine off and the chamber proven empty, pull the cocking handle completely rearward and release it. From here until it is back together, do not pull the trigger.
steps.prose: This stroke sets the hammer at its lowered, cocked position. With the hammer raised, the moving parts and the hammer group will not come out. If the trigger has been pulled after the moving parts came out, FN's answer is to put the carbine back together, cock it and start again.
steps.quote: This operation is necessary because it is only possible to remove the moving parts group and the hammer group when the hammer is at the (lowered) cocked position.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.1 Disassembling the carbine, pp.24–25
steps.warn: From now on, do not pull the trigger : the hammer would again be positioned at its (raised) decocked position.

steps.title: Barrel and upper rail forward and out
steps.action: Push down on the barrel support lock and keep it down. Move the barrel support and upper rail group slightly forward to release it, then slide it completely out of the frame.
steps.prose: It comes off in two moves: a short one that frees it, then the long slide out. If the first one will not start, the lock is not all the way down.
steps.quote: While pushing down on the barrel support lock, release the barrel support and upper rail group by moving it slightly forward and then slide it completely out of the frame.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.1 Disassembling the carbine, p.24

steps.title: Moving parts group forward and out
steps.action: Reach in through the magazine opening and push the moving parts group forward to release it. Then carefully slide it completely out of the front of the frame.
steps.prose: It is the breech block and its guide rods in one piece, and it stays in one piece. See which side has the raised surface before you put it down: that side goes back on top.
steps.quote: Release the moving parts group by pushing it forward (via the magazine opening) and then carefully slide it completely out of the frame.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.1 Disassembling the carbine, p.24; reassembly points, p.26

steps.title: Butt plate up and off
steps.action: At the rear of the frame, slide the butt plate up and off.
steps.prose: Up, not back. The hammer group comes out through the opening it uncovers.
steps.quote: At the rear, slide the butt plate up and off the frame.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.1 Disassembling the carbine, p.25

steps.title: Hammer group out of the rear
steps.action: Raise the hammer group release lever and, while you hold it up, pull the hammer group slightly rearward to release it. Then slide the group completely out of the frame.
steps.prose: If it will not move, do not lever it. The usual reason is a hammer that is up because the trigger was pulled, and the cure is to reassemble, cock it and start the strip again.
steps.quote: While raising the hammer group release lever, pull the hammer group slightly rearward in order to release it.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.1 Disassembling the carbine, p.25
steps.warn: Note that the hammer group cannot be removed if the hammer is at the (raised) decocked position.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Five groups on the bench: barrel support and upper rail, moving parts, butt plate, hammer group, and the frame with its trigger. The magazine makes six. Deep Clean covers opening the magazine.
steps.prose: FN says this is enough for a thorough cleaning, and that anything further is for an FN Recommended Service Center or a departmental armorer. Leave each group whole.
steps.quote: This level of disassembly is sufficient to perform thorough cleaning : further disassembly should only be carried out by a FN Recommended Service Center / your departmental armorer.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.1 closing note, p.25
steps.warn: It can be very dangerous to alter firing mechanism parts of this or any firearm.

steps.title: Bore: solvent, then clean rags
steps.action: Brush or spray solvent into the bore and let it work for a few minutes. Run clean flannel rags through on a cleaning rag holder until the last one comes out clean. Finish with a piece of flannel moistened with maintenance lubricant, to protect the bore until the next use. Wipe the rest of the barrel support and upper rail group with a soft cloth.
steps.prose: The film is for storage only. FN wants the bore wiped dry before you shoot, and the barrel checked for obstructions, because the smallest one can raise pressures dangerously.
steps.quote: Using a cleaning rag holder and clean rags (pieces of flannel), remove the functional lubricant, the solvent and the residues from the bore of the barrel until the last rag is clean.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §6.2 Cleaning and lubrication after firing, p.30; §6, p.29
steps.warn: Never use hydrocarbons, trichlorethylene nor ammonia : they could cause damage to your carbine !

steps.title: Carbon off the moving parts
steps.action: Take the carbon and other deposits off the moving parts group with a cleaning brush and solvent. Rinse it in a soft solvent if it needs it, and dry it with a soft cloth. Move the breech block rearward along its guide rods and clean the rods.
steps.prose: The guide rods are easy to miss, because part of each one is hidden until the breech block is moved back. FN warns that some solvents harm the carbine's finish, so ask a Service Center if you are not sure of yours.
steps.quote: Move the breech block rearward along its guide rods and then clean the guide rods.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §6.2 Cleaning and lubrication after firing, p.30; §9, p.33

steps.title: A few drops on the moving parts, and nowhere else
steps.action: Put two drops of lubricant on each guide rod, just behind the breech block, and move the breech block back and forth at least three times. Put one drop on the ejector, one on the extractor, and one at the holes of the breech block.
steps.prose: These are the only lubrication points FN gives. After firing, it names maintenance lubricant for them; before firing, that comes off and functional lubricant goes on at the same points. FN recommends Nycolube 127 CLP or an equivalent to MIL-PRF-63460. More than this collects dirt and powder residue.
steps.quote: Apply 2 drops of functional lubricant to each guide rod, just behind the breech block.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §6.1, p.29; §6.2, p.31; §9, p.33
steps.warn: Excessive lubrication of the firearm or the presence of a lubricant inside the magazine or the hammer group will have an unfavourable effect on the reliability of the firearm and the longevity of the parts.

steps.title: Hammer group: dry cloth, no lubricant
steps.action: Wipe the hammer group with a soft, dry cloth. If that is not enough, use water, and dry it again before it goes back.
steps.prose: No solvent and no oil are named for this group. Lubricant in here is what FN says can make the carbine malfunction. Leave the hammer cocked while you clean it.
steps.quote: Clean with a soft, dry cloth. If necessary, use water.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §6.2 Cleaning and lubrication after firing, p.31
steps.warn: Components of the hammer group may never be lubricated : the presence of a lubricant inside the hammer group could cause malfunctions.

steps.title: Frame and trigger group
steps.action: Wipe the frame and trigger group with a soft, dry cloth. If it needs more, use water or a soft solvent.
steps.prose: The frame is polymer and needs no lubricant. Keep your finger off the trigger while the cloth is in there: the groups go back with the hammer cocked.
steps.quote: Clean with a soft, dry cloth. If necessary, use water or a soft solvent.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §6.2 Cleaning and lubrication after firing, p.30

steps.title: Magazine: outside, dry
steps.action: Wipe the empty magazine with a soft, dry cloth. If it is very soiled, and it is not a 10-round magazine, Deep Clean shows how FN opens it.
steps.prose: The body is clear polycarbonate. FN allows water on its parts when it has been taken apart, and no solvent at any time.
steps.quote: Never use any kind of solvent on the magazine.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §6.2 Cleaning and lubrication after firing, p.31
steps.warn: Components of the magazine may never be lubricated : the presence of a lubricant inside the magazine could cause malfunctions.

steps.title: Look it over before it goes back
steps.action: Look at each group for wear, damage and corrosion, and look through the barrel to see that nothing was left in it. If something seems abnormal, report it to an FN Recommended Service Center or a departmental armorer. Do not repair it yourself.
steps.prose: FN wants the carbine checked by its Service Center every 10000 rounds or once a year, because wear and corrosion do not always show from outside.
steps.quote: If something seems abnormal, don’t hesitate to report it to a FN Recommended Service Center / your departmental armorer.
steps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §7 Taking care of the carbine, p.32
steps.warn: Never modify or repair parts of your carbine (or any other one) by yourself.

deepSteps.title: Only a 30- or 50-round magazine comes apart
deepSteps.action: Check which magazine you have. If it is the reduced-capacity 10-round magazine, stop: it cannot be disassembled, and a soft, dry cloth on the outside is its cleaning.
deepSteps.prose: FN keeps this for a magazine that is very soiled. If yours is not, wiping it is enough.
deepSteps.quote: If the magazine is very soiled, disassemble it and then clean its parts by using water. Please note that a (reduced capacity) 10-round magazine cannot be disassembled.
deepSteps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §6.2 Cleaning and lubrication after firing, p.31

deepSteps.title: Empty the magazine
deepSteps.action: With the magazine off the carbine, push the cartridges forward out of it with your thumb, one by one, until it is empty. Put the cartridges away from the bench.
deepSteps.prose: The clear body shows you what is left. Look at the lips as well as along the body before you go on.
deepSteps.quote: If the magazine is not empty, unload it by pushing the cartridges, one by one, forward with the thumb.
deepSteps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §4.5 Unloading the carbine, p.23; §5.2, p.26

deepSteps.title: Bottom lock in, bottom plate sideways
deepSteps.action: Put eye protection on. Press the magazine bottom lock with your index finger through the hole in the bottom plate. Hold it there and move the bottom plate sideways until it comes free of the magazine body.
deepSteps.prose: The plate moves sideways, and the lock has to stay pressed the whole way. Keep the bottom of the magazine pointed away from your face: as the plate clears, the lock and the spring behind it are free to move.
deepSteps.quote: While holding the magazine bottom lock in that position, move the magazine bottom plate sidewards until it is disengaged from the magazine body.
deepSteps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.2 Disassembling the magazine, pp.26–27; §1, p.9
deepSteps.warn: Take into account that the magazine bottom lock is subject to the force of the magazine follower spring.

deepSteps.title: Let the follower assembly out slowly
deepSteps.action: Keep control of the lock and carefully let the pressure off the magazine follower assembly. Then take the assembly out of the magazine body.
deepSteps.prose: Note which way round it came out. FN prints a pictogram on the side of the magazine body to help you get it back.
deepSteps.quote: Carefully release the pressure on the magazine follower assembly.
deepSteps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.2 Disassembling the magazine, p.27

deepSteps.title: Tip out the two rollers
deepSteps.action: Hold the magazine body slightly inclined and let the two rollers come out. Count two. Go no further with the magazine.
deepSteps.prose: They are loose once the follower assembly is out, so do this over a cloth. FN stops here: anything further is for its Recommended Service Center or a departmental armorer.
deepSteps.quote: Hold the magazine body slightly inclined in order to remove the 2 rollers.
deepSteps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.2 Disassembling the magazine, p.27

deepSteps.title: Clean the parts with water only
deepSteps.action: Clean the body, bottom plate, follower assembly and rollers with water. Dry every part before any of it goes back.
deepSteps.prose: Water is the only thing FN gives for the inside of the magazine. No solvent, and nothing goes back on it afterward.
deepSteps.quote: Never use any kind of solvent on the magazine. Components of the magazine may never be lubricated : the presence of a lubricant inside the magazine could cause malfunctions.
deepSteps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §6.2 Cleaning and lubrication after firing, p.31; §5.2, p.27

deepSteps.title: Rollers and follower assembly back in
deepSteps.action: Put the two rollers into the magazine body one behind the other. Put the follower assembly in, oriented the way the pictogram on the side of the body shows.
deepSteps.prose: Both are easy to get wrong by feel. Check the rollers are in line before the follower assembly covers them.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure that the 2 rollers are inserted one behind the other into the magazine body.
deepSteps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.2, reassembly points, p.27

deepSteps.title: Lock flush, plate on, check it caught
deepSteps.action: Push the magazine bottom lock in and hold it flush with the edge of the magazine body. Slide the bottom plate back on, and make sure it locks into position.
deepSteps.prose: The plate will not slide on while the lock stands proud. Once it is on, see that it cannot be moved sideways again without pressing the lock.
deepSteps.quote: The magazine bottom plate can only be slid back into position when the magazine bottom lock is pushed and held flush with the edge of the magazine body.
deepSteps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §5.2, reassembly points, p.27

deepSteps.title: No further: the rest is FN's
deepSteps.action: Take nothing else apart. The hammer group, the moving parts group, the trigger and the barrel support stay whole.
deepSteps.prose: FN gives no procedure past the field strip and the magazine. A carbine that needs more than that goes to an FN Recommended Service Center, and law enforcement to a departmental armorer.
deepSteps.quote: Like all FN firearms, your carbine should be serviced by a FN Recommended Service Center.
deepSteps.cite: FN PS90® AUTOLOADING CARBINE OWNER'S MANUAL — 1605 - PS90® - OM 3810054200 — §1, p.10; §5.1 and §5.2 closing notes, pp.25 and 27
deepSteps.warn: It can be very dangerous to alter firing mechanism parts of this or any firearm.

cleaning.name: BARREL & UPPER RAIL
tasks: Solvent into the bore by brush or spray, a few minutes to work
Clean flannel rags until the last one comes out clean
A piece of flannel moistened with maintenance lubricant for storage
The rest of the group wiped with a soft cloth
Wipe the bore dry before you shoot
⛔ Never hydrocarbons, trichlorethylene or ammonia

cleaning.name: MOVING PARTS GROUP
tasks: Carbon and deposits off with brush and solvent
Rinsed in a soft solvent if needed, dried with a soft cloth
Breech block moved rearward and the guide rods cleaned
Two drops on each guide rod, just behind the breech block
Breech block moved back and forth at least three times
One drop on the ejector, the extractor and the holes of the breech block

cleaning.name: HAMMER GROUP
tasks: Soft, dry cloth; water if necessary
⛔ Never lubricate the hammer group

cleaning.name: FRAME & MAGAZINE
tasks: Frame and trigger group with a soft, dry cloth; water or a soft solvent if necessary
Magazine with a soft, dry cloth
⛔ Never solvent on the magazine
⛔ Never lubricate the magazine

cleaning.name: HOW OFTEN
tasks: Clean and lubricate after every use, or every 2000 rounds in intensive shooting
More often with excessively dirty ammunition
Before first use, to take the preservation lubricant off
Before shooting: bore dried, storage lubricant off the moving parts, then the same few drops of functional lubricant
FN Recommended Service Center check every 10000 rounds or once a year

reassembly: Make sure every group is clean and dry. The hammer is still cocked, the magazine is off and the trigger is left alone.
Hammer group into the rear of the frame: hold its release lever at the raised position while it goes in.
Butt plate back down onto the rear of the frame.
Moving parts group into the frame with its raised surface on top.
Barrel support and upper rail group into the frame with the barrel support lock pressed.
Check that each group has locked into position.
Make sure the magazine and the chamber are really empty, then fit the empty magazine.
Point the carbine in a safe direction, set the selector at 1 and pull the trigger to decock the hammer. Set the selector back at S.
fncheck: With no ammunition anywhere near the bench — FN says never to test the mechanical function with live ammunition — check the chamber by eye and by touch before any trigger press. Take the magazine off again. The cocking handle should run completely rearward and the moving parts should go fully forward when you release it. With the hammer cocked and the selector at S, the trigger cannot be operated. At 1, pointed in a safe direction, one press drops the hammer. Set the selector back at S. An empty magazine should lock in when you push firmly on its rear part, and stay put when you pull it upwards. If something is wrong, FN's list is: selector not at S, carbine cocked, correctly reassembled, magazine opening and chamber clear, inside not heavily soiled. If it is still not right, it goes to a Service Center before it is fired.
